concerns.text: T106 mandates Adapter records carry `confidence_score` and `exclude_from_stats: true`, but `experiment_log.schema.yaml` declares `additionalProperties: false` and defines neither field. A T106 implementer cannot satisfy both the task and the schema; T112's validation would then fail on the very artifacts T106 is verified by. Either the schema must be extended or the fields moved to a sidecar file — the task as written is not executable.

T112 validates `classifier_training_data.json` against `contracts/trajectory.schema.yaml`, but T103's records (trajectory_id, turn_text, label, confidence_score, threshold_used) are not ConflictTrajectory objects — they will never validate. The verification step is unexecutable as specified; the training-data file needs its own schema or must be validated structurally.

T103's label vocabulary is {'high_reactivity', 'cultural_friction', 'neutral'} while the experiment-log schema's `injected_state` examples and T105/T106 use 'escalating'/'cultural-friction'/'neutral-monitoring'. No task defines the mapping from classifier labels to injected_state values, so the T105/T106 implementer cannot deterministically produce schema-conformant `injected_state` strings from T103's classifier output.

T101 (and T112) reference `contracts/trajectory.schema.yaml`, but the contract directory contains `dataset.schema.yaml` (same content, different filename). An implementer following the task literally will fail to find the file. Reconcile the filename.

T110's `stats_report.json` keys (test_type, statistic, p_value, is_significant, effect_size) do not match `report.schema.yaml`'s required structure (llm_id, comparison{mean_diff, p_value, is_significant, effect_size, test_type, normality_p_value}, correction_applied), yet T110's verification says the report 'validates against contracts/report.schema.yaml'. Specify the artifact shape (per-LLM array vs single object) and align the key list so the verification is executable.

T105's verification ('running one model on 3 trajectories') does not name the command or how the subset is selected; T106 supports `--seed` but T105 gives no invocation. Add the concrete command (e.g. `python code/experiments/runner.py --models <one> --n 3`) so the check is deterministic.
